title: 第9章 四书五经第10章 仙学开讲
content_zh:
仙塾是仙学启蒙之地，修仙也有四书五经。
四书：子曰，我闻，太玄，易数。
五经：阵图、符箓、丹鼎、天工、祝由。
吴燃灯认真研读起来。
仙学浩如烟海，博大精深，能成就飞升伟业的学问，必是这世间最大的学问无疑，蕴含着超脱天地的道理。
他一时间读起来，也觉得晦涩难懂。
但他也没奢望一下子，弄懂诸多奥秘，只求通读一遍，对仙学仙道有个大体认知即可。
“子曰：“吾道一以贯之。””
“如是我闻：佛在舍卫国……”
“玄之又玄，众妙之门！视不可见，谓之：太玄！”
一行行玄妙文字在眼前浮现，眉心学无止境命格连连悸动，闪烁不止，热得发烫，隐隐约约中吴燃灯眼前隐现诸多幻象，诸天诸佛端坐云端之上，天地至理，天人妙音，让人为之神往。
【子曰：入门（5100）】
【我闻：入门（6100）】
【太玄：入门（2100）】
【易数：入门（1100）】
……
命格上一行行墨痕浮现，仙学的四书五经都已被录入其上，尽在吴燃灯心头回荡，不会忘却。
仙学帷幕也被他掀开一角，露出了真容。
原来仙学流派众多，各家各派修行方式各有不同。
这四书经典，分别讲的就是释儒道三家的修仙学问，再加上一门格物求理的求道之学，易数。

《子曰》，这是儒道的功法，记载了儒道诸圣口述的学问，讲究以“吾道一以贯之”，以诚信正念。
修仙者悟此句，以“守一”为心法根基。持剑则剑心归一，炼丹则丹火归一，符箓则笔意归一。
故入门儒修必修《子曰·定静章》，其中“学而不思则罔”解为“盲修则气散，思悟则神凝”，“温故而知新”注“复盘旧法，方得新境”，字字皆为定心要诀。
《我闻》则为佛门心法，记载了弟子对诸佛的禅理，以“闻、思、修”为三要。
弟子修行时需先诵“如是我闻”四字真言，澄心净念，再观想佛陀说法时的宝相，其文简奥，首言“诸法空相”，谓功法不重灵力积蓄，而重“心印”传承，悟六神通，举手投足自带祥和气，邪祟不近。
《太玄》观气，为道德之门，玄之又玄，众妙之门。
此篇专论天地元气流动。修士观气如观纹，能辨“青气主生，白气主杀，紫气主贵”。初阶见气如薄雾，中阶见气如水流，高阶见气如星轨。书中插画绘“太玄八卦图”，每卦对应一气，转动卦盘可测气之盛衰，乃外出历练必备。
这释儒道三法，与前世颇有共通之处，吴燃灯心有领会，入门倒也极快，命格上的学习进度也肉眼可见的增长，很快就双双破10。
【子曰：入门（13100）】
【我闻：入门（12100）】
【太玄：入门（10100）】
而最令吴燃灯感到玄奇，进度也是最慢的，就是四书最后一书，《易数》！
《易数》，源出先天八卦，以“观变、应机、通神”为宗，其术简而奥，核心为三十六爻变，暗藏天地运行之理。
修此术者需先明“数生象，象生势”，以六十四卦配天干地支观天象，察地脉，将星轨、山形、人事皆化为爻象记于龟甲或蓍草。初学时以三枚铜钱起卦，掷六次成一卦，依爻辞断吉凶——若遇“潜龙勿用”，则知时机未到，需藏锋守拙；逢“飞龙在天”，便晓运势鼎盛，可顺势而为。
进阶则弃铜钱，以自身气血为引，于掌心布卦。指尖凝气画爻，阳爻如剑破云，阴爻似水流柔，刚柔相济时，周遭灵气会随卦象聚散，形成“卦场”。
比如布“坎为水”卦，可引水汽化雨；演“离为火”象，能聚热生温。然卦无定数，变爻乃关键，一爻变动，全局皆改，故修者需炼“随机应变”之心，临事不慌，方能从变数中寻生机。
此术最忌“拘数”，若死搬爻辞，不知通变，卦象便会显“凶咎”，反噬自身。
需知“数随心动，心合天道”，待修至“数外无象，象外无神”之境，无需起卦，抬眼所见皆为天机，抬手所动皆合数理，可趋吉避凶于无形，甚至能以己之数改他人之运，此谓“易数通神”。
不止是八卦玄机，其中还涉及诸多数学之理，至深至奥。
“果然大道殊途同归！”
content_en:
The Immortal School is the place where immortality is enlightened, and there are also four books and five classics for cultivating immortality.
Four Books: Confucius said, I heard that Taixuan is easy to count.
The Five Classics: formation map, talisman, alchemy tripod, Tiangong, and Zhuyou.
Wu Randeng studied it carefully.
Immortal learning is vast, broad and profound. The knowledge that can achieve great achievements in ascension must be the greatest knowledge in the world. It contains principles that transcend heaven and earth.
Even when he read it, he felt it was obscure and difficult to understand.
But he didn't expect to understand many mysteries in one go. He just wanted to read it through once and have a general understanding of the Immortal School and Immortal Way.
"The Master said: "My way is consistent. ""
"This is what I heard: The Buddha is in the country of Savatthi..."
"Mysterious and mysterious, the door to all mysteries! Invisible, it is called: Tai Xuan!"
Lines of mysterious words appeared in front of his eyes, and the endless life patterns on his brows were throbbing, flickering, and burning. Many illusions vaguely appeared in front of Wu Randeng's eyes. The gods and Buddhas were sitting on the clouds.
[Confucius said: Getting Started (5100)]
[I heard: Getting Started (6100)]
[Tai Xuan: Getting Started (2100)]
[Easy Numbers: Getting Started (1100)]
…
Lines of ink marks appeared on the fate chart, and the Four Books and Five Classics of Immortal Studies had been recorded on them, which echoed in Wu Randeng's heart and would never be forgotten.
He also lifted a corner of the curtain of immortality, revealing his true appearance.
It turns out that there are many schools of immortality, and each school has its own different practice methods.
These four classics respectively talk about the knowledge of cultivating immortals from the three schools of Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism, plus a study of seeking Tao through studying things and seeking principles. It is easy to count.
"Confucius said", this is a Confucian and Taoist practice. It records the oral knowledge of Confucian and Taoist sages. It pays attention to "my way is consistent" and to be honest and righteous.
Immortal cultivators understand this sentence and take "keeping oneness" as the foundation of their mind. Holding the sword will bring the sword's heart to one, refining the elixir will bring the elixir and fire to one, and using the talisman will bring the meaning of the brush to one.
Therefore, it is compulsory for beginners to study Confucianism in "Zi Yue Ding Jing Zhang", in which "learning without thinking leads to indifference" is interpreted as "blind practice will cause the energy to disperse, and thinking will lead to concentration", "reviewing the old and knowing the new" notes "revisiting the old method, only then can you gain a new realm", every word is the key to calming down.
"I Hear" is the Buddhist mental method, which records the disciples' Zen principles about the Buddhas, with "hearing, contemplation, and cultivation" as the three essentials.
When practicing, disciples need to first recite the four-character mantra "Thus I have heard" to clear their minds and thoughts, and then visualize the treasures and appearances of the Buddha when he preaches. The text is simple and concise, and the first sentence is "all dharmas are empty", which means that the practice does not focus on the accumulation of spiritual power, but on the inheritance of "heart seal", realize the six supernatural powers, carry a peaceful aura with every move, and prevent evil spirits from approaching.
"Tai Xuan" Observation of Qi is the door of morality, mystery and mystery, and the door of all mysteries.
This article is dedicated to the flow of vitality between heaven and earth. A monk observes Qi as he observes patterns, and can tell that "green Qi is responsible for life, white Qi is responsible for killing, and purple Qi is responsible for nobleness". At the initial level, the energy is like mist, at the intermediate level, it is like water flow, and at the advanced level, it is like star trails. The illustrations in the book depict the "Tai Xuan Bagua Diagram". Each hexagram corresponds to a qi. The rise and fall of qi can be measured by turning the hexagram disk, which is a must-have for outdoor experience.
These three methods of Confucianism and Taoism have quite a lot in common with the previous life. Wu Randeng understood it in his heart, and he got started very quickly. His progress in learning about life horoscopes also increased visibly, and both of them soon exceeded 10.
[Confucius said: Getting Started (13100)]
[I smell: Getting Started (12100)]
[Tai Xuan: Getting Started (10100)]
The one that struck Wu Randeng as the most mysterious and progressed the slowest was the last of the Four Books, "The Book of Changes"!
"Yisu" originated from the innate Bagua, and is based on "observation of changes, response to opportunities, and communication with the gods". Its technique is simple and profound, with the core of thirty-six lines of changes, which hides the principles of the movement of heaven and earth.
Those who practice this technique need to first understand that "numbers create images, and images create momentum", use the sixty-four hexagrams with the heavenly stems and earthly branches to observe the celestial phenomena, observe the earth's veins, and turn the star paths, mountain shapes, and people into lines of images and record them on tortoise shells or yarrow. When you first start learning, use three copper coins to start a hexagram, throw it six times to form a hexagram, and judge the good or bad according to the lines - if you encounter "Don't use the hidden dragon", you know that the time has not come yet, and you need to hide your front and guard your back;If the dragon is in the sky, you will know that your fortune will be prosperous and you can follow the trend.
To advance, abandon copper coins, use your own Qi and blood as a guide, and create hexagrams in the palm of your hand. The fingertips gather energy to draw lines. The yang lines are like swords breaking through clouds, and the yin lines are like soft water. When hardness and softness are combined, the surrounding spiritual energy will gather and disperse according to the hexagram images, forming a "hexagram field".
For example, the hexagram "Kan is water" can induce water to vaporize and turn into rain; the hexagram "Li is fire" can gather heat and generate warmth. However, the hexagram has no fixed number, and changing the line is the key. If one line changes, the whole situation will change. Therefore, practitioners need to practice the heart of "adapting to changes" and not panic when things happen, so that they can find hope from the variables.
The most taboo in this technique is "restriction on numbers". If you insist on copying the lines without knowing how to adapt them, the hexagrams will appear "sinful" and backfire on you.
It is necessary to know that "numbering follows the movement of the heart, and the heart is in harmony with the way of heaven." Once you have cultivated to the state of "there is no image outside the number, there is no god outside the image", there is no need to use hexagrams, everything you see when you raise your eyes is heaven's secrets, and everything you raise your hands is in accordance with the principles of mathematics. You can seek good luck and avoid evil in the invisible, and you can even change the luck of others with your own numbers. This is called "easy to count and communicate with the gods".
It is not only the mysteries of Bagua, but also involves many mathematical principles, which are profound and profound.
"Sure enough, there are different paths leading to the same destination! "
